title: Scaling Enterprise-Grade RAG: Lessons from Legal Frontier - Calvin Qi (Harvey), Chang She (Lance)
talk_summary: A Harvey engineer and LanceDB's CEO describe building large-scale legal RAG: complex multi-part queries, huge domain corpora, and the need for flexible retrieval infrastructure. The most transferable content is their eval-driven development philosophy and tiered eval strategy; the rest is LanceDB product marketing.

takeaways.technique: Tiered eval pyramid (expert review → expert-labeled criteria → automated metrics)
takeaways.what_they_do: They run evals at multiple fidelity/cost levels: expensive expert human review of outputs, mid-tier expert-curated labeled criteria evaluated automatically, and cheap deterministic metrics (retrieval precision/recall, right folder/section, keyword presence) for fast iteration.
takeaways.evidence_quote: there's no silver bullet eval, but we have like a whole range of them of like different task depths and complexities

takeaways.technique: Eval-driven development as the primary investment
takeaways.what_they_do: They explicitly deprioritize fancy agentic algorithms in favor of building evaluation harnesses first, so changes can be validated quickly in a domain engineers don't natively know.
takeaways.evidence_quote: investing in eval driven development is a huge huge key to building these systems and making sure they're good

takeaways.technique: Decompose complex queries into typed sub-needs (semantic, filter, keyword, multi-part)
takeaways.what_they_do: They analyze query structure to separate semantic intent, implicit filters (dates), exact ID/keyword matches, and multi-regulation references, then route each part to the appropriate retrieval mechanism.

takeaways.technique: Single source of truth to avoid sync glue work
takeaways.what_they_do: They argue teams waste effort keeping copies of data in sync across systems, and push storing all data (blobs + scalars + embeddings) in one table/format.
takeaways.evidence_quote: they're spending a lot of their time and effort just sort of keeping those um pieces glued together and in sync
